styles.blurb: The Alhambra, the Generalife and the Nasrid palaces.

styles.label: Tapas

styles.label: Romance
styles.blurb: Sunset views over the Alhambra and whitewashed lanes in Albayzin.

stays.why: Central base near Plaza Nueva and the Cathedral. Easy walks, many restaurants, but busy and noisy at night.
Historic hillside quarter facing the Alhambra. Great views and romantic streets, but steep and uneven. Bring comfortable shoes.
Calm former Jewish quarter with local bars and a relaxed feel. Quieter than Centro and close to the historic core.
Cave-house neighbourhood known for flamenco. Atmospheric, but far from the centre and best reached by bus or taxi at night.

food: Tapas often come free with a drink in many bars. Order a drink and ask what comes with it; check on the day.
Try the local dish of habas con jamón (broad beans with ham) and piononos, a small rolled sponge cake.
Eat early or book ahead for dinner. Many kitchens open around 20:00 to 21:00 and fill quickly in high season.
Visit a covered market such as Mercado San Agustín for fresh produce and cheap snacks.
Plan a tapas crawl in Centro or Realejo, where bars are close together and walkable.
more_time: Mountain fans: take a day trip to the Sierra Nevada. Check bus times and snow conditions before you go.
Villages and walks: visit the white villages of the Alpujarras by bus or tour. Check services, as they run less often.
Wider day trip: visit Córdoba or Sevilla for more Moorish and Andalusian history. Check train or coach times in advance.

recommend.why: Two nights give you a full day at the Alhambra, time in Albayzin and an evening of tapas without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: Cold, with highs around 13°C and lows near 3°C. Rain on about 7 days. Bring warm layers for the Alhambra.
Feb: Mild but chilly, highs around 15°C and lows near 4°C. Rain on about 7 days. Good for quiet sightseeing.
Mar: Spring starts. Highs around 17°C and lows near 6°C. Rain on about 12 days, so pack a light jacket.
Apr: Pleasant, highs around 20°C and lows near 8°C. Rain on about 9 days. Good for walking the hills.
May: Warm and sunny, highs around 25°C and lows near 12°C. Rain on about 6 days. Book Alhambra tickets early.
Jun: Hot, highs around 30°C and lows near 16°C. Rain on about 3 days. Visit the Alhambra early in the morning.
Jul: Very hot, highs around 35°C and lows near 21°C. Rain on about 2 days. Plan indoor visits for midday.
Aug: Very hot, highs around 35°C and lows near 21°C. Rain on about 2 days. Evenings are the best time to be outdoors.
Sep: Still warm, highs around 29°C and lows near 16°C. Rain on about 4 days. A good month for sightseeing.
Oct: Mild, highs around 24°C and lows near 12°C. Rain on about 7 days. One of the best months to visit.
Nov: Cool, highs around 17°C and lows near 7°C. Rain on about 8 days. Quieter streets and easier hotel prices.
Dec: Cold, highs around 15°C and lows near 5°C. Rain on about 6 days. Pack warm clothes for evening walks.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate with hot summers, cold winters and a clear shoulder season in spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: April to May and October
items.text: Highs around 20–25°C with fewer crowds. Ideal for the Alhambra and long walks in the old quarters.

items.title: Hot summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs around 30–35°C and lows near 16–21°C. Visit sights early or late and rest at midday.

items.title: Cold winter (December to February)
items.text: Highs around 13–15°C and lows near 3–5°C. Bring a warm jacket for evenings and early mornings.

items.title: Rain is most likely in March and November
items.text: Around 8–12 rainy days in those months. Pack a light waterproof and check the forecast before day trips.

items.title: Sunny most of the year
items.text: Rain falls on only 2–4 days in June to August. Sunscreen and a hat matter from late spring onward.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable shoes with good grip for steep, uneven streets. Layers for cool evenings, plus sun protection in summer.

transit.best: Walk the old quarters, and use city buses for the hills and the Alhambra.

modes.text: One metro line runs in Granada. A single ticket costs about €1.65 (Nov 2024). A rechargeable green travel card costs €1.50 at tobacco shops and needs at least €5 of credit.
Alhambra Buses cover most sights: C30 to the Alhambra, C31 to Albayzin and C34 to Sacromonte. Each trip costs €1.60 (Nov 2024). Multi-trip cards cost €5, €10 or €20.
Taxis are easy to find. Ride apps such as Uber or Cabify are available; check locally.
Driving in the centre is restricted, with camera-enforced limits. Park outside the historic core or use a garage such as Parking HH Maristas.
Walking is the best way to see the old quarters, but streets are steep, narrow and uneven. Buses help on the hills.
No ferry service applies to Granada.
